problem: Let ${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2\end{aligned}]$ and ${v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]$ be eigenvectors of a matrix $A.$ Find the decoupling matrix of the differential equation ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t).$

activity_context.topic_title: Solving Homogeneous Systems of ODEs With Distinct Eigenvalues

feedback.problem:
Find the substitution that will decouple the following system of differential equations: 

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}(t)={x}_{1}(t) \\ {x}_{2}^{′}(t)=-2{x}_{1}(t)-{x}_{2}(t)\end{aligned}
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
We need to find the eigenvalues and the eigenvectors of the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -2 & -1\end{aligned}].$

- Since $A$ is lower-triangular, the eigenvalues are 

$$
{\lambda }_{1}=1\,\text{and}\,{\lambda }_{2}=-1.
$$

- Let's go through the process of finding the eigenvectors.

- For ${\lambda }_{1}=1,$ we get 

$$
A-{\lambda }_{1}I=[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ -2 & -2\end{aligned}]∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

So, we get an eigenvector 
${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$

- For ${\lambda }_{2}=-1,$ we get 

$$
A-{\lambda }_{2}I=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ -2 & 0\end{aligned}]∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

So, we get an eigenvector 
${v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$

Therefore, we have $E=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}].$

Finally, the change of variables that decouples the system is given by $x(t)=Eu(t)$, or equivalently,

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(t)=-{u}_{1}(t) \\ {x}_{2}(t)={u}_{1}(t)+{u}_{2}(t).\end{aligned}
$$
